meta.title: Government jobs as a share of all jobs, by county and town

source.label: U.S. Census Bureau, LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES 8), Workplace Area Characteristics, 2024

meta.what: Jobs counted where people work (all jobs, JT00). Government is all jobs less private jobs (JT02); federal is JT04; state and local is the rest. Private jobs at large firms are those at employers with 500 or more employees nationwide (CFS05), so a chain store counts.
meta.why: County Business Patterns leaves out government. This line names no employer but shows how much of an area's work is public: school districts, counties, hospital districts, prisons, universities.
limits: LODES adds noise to small-area counts to protect confidentiality, so a town figure is an estimate.
Some state employees are reported at an administrative address, not where they work, so a county with a large state office can look high and its neighbours low.
Leaves out the self-employed, uniformed military and some federal security agencies.
Towns are the 2020 Census place boundaries in the LODES crosswalk; jobs outside any place count only to the county.

In the 2024 file about 23,000 state and local jobs moved to Denver from Adams, Arapahoe, Mesa, Boulder, Pueblo and Larimer counties against the 2023 file, with no matching change in total jobs: this looks like state employees reported at a Denver administrative address, so year-to-year changes in a county's government share are not evidence by themselves.
meta.shown: true where the share is published; otherwise why_not says why.
